records.subject: Get your team moving with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Felix,

A reminder that your Wrenfield workspace is ready whenever you are -- creating one real project is the easiest way to see what it's for.

Warmly,
Elena Kelly

records.subject: Welcome to Wrenfield, Maple Collective!
records.body:
Hi Felix,

Thanks for signing up for Wrenfield. Two things that help teams get going: create a project, and invite at least one teammate from Account Settings -> Members.

Happy to answer anything.

Best,
Nadia Goldberg

decisions.rationale: Day 6 of 14, no project, no invite, no milestone despite three touches (email:dee0c3b2, 9871a551, 52eeed59). Customer explicitly said they're still evaluating and asked for another week (email:0566cb08), which pushes any action past the day-14 window. No tickets or product questions signal low engagement.

draft.subject: Re: Quick check-in from Wrenfield
draft.body:
Hi Felix,

Thanks for the straight answer — totally fair to take another week to decide, and I won't crowd you in the meantime.

One thing that usually makes the decision easier: projects are the main organizing unit in Wrenfield, and tasks live inside them, so setting up one real project tends to show quickly whether it fits how your team works. If it's useful, I'm happy to help you get that first project shaped around an actual piece of Maple Collective work — just reply and I'll take it from there.

Best,
Nadia
